extracted.intended_audience: researchers and data scientists conducting large-scale name-based racial inference (bibliometrics, scientometrics, social science, public policy researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for inferring perceived race from personal names in large-scale datasets (e.g., authors in bibliographic databases). Focuses on choice of name features, reference datasets, modeling choices (thresholds vs continuous), validation, and how methodological choices introduce bias across racial/ethnic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully consider algorithmic bias when inferring race
rubrics_metrics.description: As with any other algorithm, the process of racial inference can generate biases if it is not carefully considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat racial inference methods as potentially biased algorithms; explicitly evaluate and report biases introduced by modeling choices rather than assuming outputs are neutral. Design analyses with awareness that methodological choices can distort group-level estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose and document appropriate reference datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: We use information from the U.S. Census and mortgage applications to infer the race of U.S. affiliated authors in the Web of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference data (e.g., Census family-name distributions, mortgage-application given-name data) influence inference results. Researchers should select datasets appropriate to the target population, document their sources, and assess how differing reference sources affect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both given (first) and family (last) names and assess their relative contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: We estimate the effects of using given and family names...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate information from both given and family names rather than relying on one alone; analyze weight distributions for given vs family names (e.g., see 'Given names weight distribution by given and family name skewness'). Report how each name component contributes to inferred probabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hard threshold approaches or evaluate their bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold approaches underestimate Black authors and overestimate White authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that assigning a single race when a probability exceeds a threshold is harmless. If using thresholds, quantify how thresholds affect the composition of retrieved groups (coverage and share) and be aware that thresholds can systematically under- or over-represent certain groups. Consider reporting sensitivity across thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer continuous probability distributions or fractional counting over binary thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: We estimate the effects of ... thresholds or continuous distributions, and imputation. (Figure captions: 'Fractional counting on family names for comparison.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use continuous probabilistic outputs (e.g., use probabilities or fractional counts) to reflect uncertainty rather than forcing categorical assignments. Fractional counting can reduce bias introduced by hard classification and better capture ambiguous or mixed-origin names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use imputation carefully to handle missing/ambiguous cases
rubrics_metrics.description: We estimate the effects of ... imputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imputing missing or low-confidence cases, document imputation methods and examine how imputation changes group estimates. Test multiple imputation strategies and report their effects on downstream analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manually validate algorithmic racial categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Fig 1. Manual validation of racial categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform manual (human) validation of a sample of inferred labels to assess accuracy, misclassification patterns, and to calibrate automated methods. Report validation procedures, sample sizes, and inter-annotator agreement if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and report validity by race/ethnicity subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Our results demonstrate that the validity of name-based inference varies by race/ethnicity...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not report only aggregate accuracy metrics. Provide group-specific performance (e.g., precision, recall, calibration) because methods may perform unevenly across racial/ethnic groups, leading to differential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate retrieval/coverage trade-offs when choosing thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Fig 3. Changes in groups share, and people retrieved, by threshold. The evolution of thresholds between 0 and 1 ... detail on thresholds between 0.9 and 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adjusting thresholds, quantify how many individuals are classified (coverage) and how group shares change. Present plots or tables showing coverage vs threshold so readers can see trade-offs between confidence and representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulate name-component skewness to test sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fig 2. Given names weight distribution by given and family name skewness. Simulated data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simulations that vary the relative informativeness or skewness of given vs family names to explore model robustness. Simulation studies help reveal how sensitive inferences are to population name-structure assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for population heterogeneity such as temporary visa holders / international authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Fig 6. Proportion of Temporary Visa Holders by racial group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that sub-populations (e.g., temporary visa holders, recent immigrants) may have name distributions that do not align with reference datasets; explicitly analyze and report such subgroups because they can distort inferred racial composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare alternative modeling approaches (e.g., family-name fractional counting) for robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fig 4. Resulting distribution on different models with 90% threshold. Fractional counting on family names for comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and compare multiple inference strategies (thresholded categorical assignments, continuous probabilities, fractional counting, family-name vs given-name models) and show how conclusions change across methods to ensure robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclude with explicit recommendations and promote systematic, less-biased investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: We conclude with recommendations to avoid potential biases. This article lays the foundation for more systematic and less-biased investigations into racial disparities in science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After analysis, provide concrete methodological recommendations, document limitations, and encourage standardized practices for name-based inference to reduce bias in studies of racial disparities.
